documents: Every checkout mutation carries an idempotency key derived from the cart revision. Replaying a request with the same key returns the stored receipt rather than charging again. The key is namespaced per storefront, so a cart moved between storefronts cannot collide with its own earlier receipt.
Money is a minor-unit integer everywhere. Rounding happens once, at the tax boundary, using banker's rounding; never round inside a line-item loop.

A refund writes a compensating entry to the refund ledger. Nothing is ever deleted from the ledger, so a reconciliation run can replay it end to end. The ledger is append-only and idempotent per refund reference.
Address validation is advisory. A shopper may override a failed validation, and the override is recorded on the order for the fulfilment team.
Inventory is reserved optimistically for fifteen minutes. An expired reservation is swept by the reaper job, which emits a restock event.
The pricing engine is pure: it takes a cart snapshot and returns a quote. It never reads the clock, so a quote is reproducible from its snapshot alone.
Discount stacking is resolved by precedence, not by order of application. Two discounts at the same precedence are an authoring error and fail the quote.
Gift cards settle before card payments. A partial gift-card settlement leaves the remainder on the card authorisation.
Shipping quotes are cached per postcode prefix for one hour. A carrier outage invalidates the prefix rather than the whole cache.
Tax jurisdictions come from the fulfilment address, never the billing address. A cross-border order splits into per-jurisdiction subtotals.
Order state transitions are append-only. The current state is a fold over the transition log, so a bad transition can be corrected by appending, never by editing.
Webhook delivery retries with jitter for twenty-four hours. A permanently failing endpoint is parked and reported, not dropped silently.
Card authorisations expire after seven days. An order that has not shipped by then is re-authorised, which may fail and cancel the order.
The cart is anonymous until checkout. Merging an anonymous cart into an account cart keeps the higher quantity per line, never the sum.
Fraud scoring runs asynchronously. A high score holds fulfilment but never blocks the payment, so the shopper sees a normal confirmation.
Product copy is localised per storefront. A missing translation falls back to the storefront default, and the fallback is logged once per key per day.
Search indexing is eventual. A newly published product may be missing from search for up to a minute, which the storefront must not treat as an error.
Subscription renewals are scheduled from the anniversary, not from the last successful charge, so a failed month does not shift the whole schedule.
Invoices are immutable once issued. A correction is a credit note referencing the original invoice number.
Customer exports are generated offline and delivered by signed link. The link expires in an hour and is single use.
Abandoned-cart mail is capped at two messages per shopper per week, across all storefronts, and honours the marketing opt-out.
The admin audit log records the acting user, the before value and the after value. An entry with no before value is a creation, not a missing field.
segments: I threaded the idempotency key through the checkout mutation. Replaying a request with the same key returns the stored receipt rather than charging again, which is exactly what the rule asks for.
The cart revision is what the key is derived from, so a genuine edit produces a new key and a retry does not.
Wrote a test that replays one idempotency key three times and asserts a single charge.
The refund path now writes a compensating entry to the refund ledger rather than reversing the original row.
Nothing is deleted from the ledger, so the nightly reconciliation replays it end to end and still balances.
I left the reconciliation job alone; it already folds the ledger, so the compensating entry lands in the right period.
The ledger reference column already existed and was unused, so there is no migration.
Ran the suite: 84 tests pass. The two flaky payment tests were flaky before this too.
Next thing I would look at is the receipt renderer, which still formats money as a float.
Also renamed the handler for clarity; it was called `doCheckout`, which said nothing.
The storefront copy is untouched, and so is the admin.
I skimmed the carrier integration but did not change it - the timeout there is generous.
One question before I go further: should a partially shipped order be refundable at all?
The staging deploy is green and the smoke script passes.
Logging is unchanged apart from one debug line I removed.
There is a stale TODO in the mailer about template versioning; I left it.
The lint run flagged two unused imports in the file I touched, and I removed them.
Nothing in this change touches the search index or the product feed.
I did not bump any dependency.
Happy to split this into two commits if you would rather review the test separately.

documents: The watchdog is kicked from the supervisor task only. A worker that kicks the watchdog hides its own deadlock, which is the failure the watchdog exists to catch. The supervisor reads every worker's liveness flag before it kicks.
CAN frames are little-endian with a two-byte sequence counter. A gap in the counter is a dropped frame and must be reported, never interpolated.
The bootloader validates the image signature before erasing the application slot, so a bad image leaves the running firmware intact.
Flash writes are page aligned. An unaligned write is a programming error and traps rather than silently rounding the address.
The scheduler is cooperative. A task that runs longer than its budget is logged with its worst-case duration at the next tick, since there is no preemption to fall back on.
Sensor calibration lives in the config page and survives a firmware update. Erasing it requires the explicit factory-reset command.
Interrupt handlers push into a lock-free ring and return. All parsing happens in task context, so a burst cannot stall the bus.
The bus is terminated at both physical ends only. A stub longer than thirty centimetres is out of spec and shows up as intermittent CRC errors.
Time comes from the monotonic tick, never from the RTC. The RTC is for timestamps in logs and nothing else, because it can step backwards after a resynchronisation.
The heartbeat frame carries the uptime and the last reset cause. A reset cause of zero means the field was never populated, not a clean boot.
Firmware version is a semantic triple plus the build hash. The hash is what a field report is matched against, since the triple can be rebuilt.
Diagnostic logging is off in release builds. Turning it on changes timing enough to hide the race it is usually turned on to find.
The motor controller is disabled on any bus silence longer than a hundred milliseconds. Silence is a fault, not an idle state.
Non-volatile counters are written with a two-slot alternating scheme, so a reset during the write leaves the previous value readable.
The debug UART is receive-only in the field. A writable console on shipped hardware is a way in, and there is no authentication on it.
Stack usage is measured by painting the stack at boot and reading the high-water mark. Every task reports its margin at shutdown.
Temperature derating starts at eighty degrees and is linear to the cutout. The curve is a table, not a formula, so it can be changed without a code review.
Over-the-air updates resume from the last acknowledged chunk. A restarted transfer that starts from zero indicates a corrupted manifest.
The fault log is a circular buffer of sixty-four entries. The oldest entry is overwritten, and the overwrite count is itself recorded.
Board revisions are read from three strapping pins. An unknown combination halts at boot rather than guessing a pinout.
The current sense amplifier saturates before the fuse opens, so a saturated reading is treated as an overcurrent even though the number is wrong.
Unit tests run on the host against a simulated bus. Timing-dependent behaviour is tested on hardware, in the soak rig, never on the host.
segments: Moved the kick into the supervisor task. A worker that kicks the watchdog hides its own deadlock, which is the whole reason the rule exists.
That immediately surfaced the stall in the parser task, which had been kicking from inside its own loop for months.
The supervisor now checks each worker's liveness flag before it kicks, and logs which worker was late.
I left the tick source alone: it is already the monotonic tick, and the RTC is only used for log timestamps.
Measured the worst-case supervisor duration at four hundred microseconds, well inside its budget, and it is logged at the next tick.
The scheduler is still cooperative, so a task over its budget shows up as a duration line rather than as a preemption.
The soak rig ran overnight with no watchdog resets, where the old build reset roughly every two hours.
No change to the bootloader or to the flash layout, so field units can take this as a normal update.
The one thing I am unsure about is whether the supervisor should kick when a worker is late, or let the reset happen.
Added a soak-rig assertion on the reset cause so a regression shows up as a failing run.
I did not touch the derating table or the current sense path.
The debug UART stayed receive-only; nothing here needed a console.
Stack high-water marks are unchanged within noise.
Host tests all pass, and I added one for the liveness flag.
No new dependency, and no change to the build hash scheme.
The fault log format is untouched.
I read the board revision code while I was in there and left it alone.
Nothing in this change is timing dependent on the host side.
Happy to run a second soak with logging on if you want the timing evidence.
The diff is about sixty lines, most of it the new liveness flag.

documents: Nigdy nie przekazuj `echo` do `pbcopy`. Uzyj `printf`, zeby usunac znak nowej linii doklejany przez terminal.
Kazda migracja bazy musi byc odwracalna. Migracja bez skryptu wycofania nie przechodzi przegladu kodu.
Logi produkcyjne nie moga zawierac danych osobowych. Identyfikator uzytkownika jest dopuszczalny, adres pocztowy nie.
Zadanie cykliczne uruchamiamy z blokada rozproszona. Dwa procesy wykonujace to samo zadanie licza wynik dwa razy.
Testy jednostkowe nie moga siegac do sieci. Zamiast tego uzywamy atrapy klienta protokolu.
Konfiguracja pochodzi ze zmiennych srodowiskowych. Wartosc wpisana w kodzie jest bledem, nawet jesli to wartosc domyslna.
Kolejka wiadomosci gwarantuje dostarczenie co najmniej raz. Odbiorca musi byc idempotentny, bo powtorzenie jest normalne.
Nazwy tabel sa w liczbie mnogiej, nazwy kolumn w pojedynczej. Skrot w nazwie kolumny wymaga komentarza w schemacie.
Blad walidacji zwracamy jako liste, nie jako pierwszy napotkany problem. Uzytkownik poprawia formularz raz, nie osiem razy.
Zaleznosci przypinamy do dokladnej wersji. Zakres wersji w pliku blokady jest bledem narzedzia, nie decyzja.
Klucz szyfrujacy rotujemy co kwartal. Stary klucz zostaje do odszyfrowania, ale nie sluzy do zapisu.
Kazdy punkt koncowy interfejsu ma limit zapytan. Punkt bez limitu jest wektorem przeciazenia.
Zdarzenia domenowe nazywamy w czasie przeszlym. Nazwa w trybie rozkazujacym opisuje polecenie, nie zdarzenie.
Kopie zapasowe odtwarzamy probnie raz w miesiacu. Kopia, ktorej nikt nie odtworzyl, nie jest kopia.
Wdrozenie odbywa sie za flaga funkcji. Wlaczenie flagi jest osobna decyzja, odwracalna bez wdrozenia.
Zapytania do bazy w petli sa zabronione. Pobieramy dane jednym zapytaniem i grupujemy w pamieci.
Strefa czasowa w bazie to zawsze UTC. Przeliczenie na strefe uzytkownika nalezy do warstwy prezentacji.
Pliki uzytkownika trafiaja do magazynu obiektowego, nigdy do systemu plikow serwera. Serwer jest wymienny.
Metryki opisujemy jednostka w nazwie. Metryka bez jednostki jest liczba, ktorej nikt nie umie zinterpretowac.
Przegladu kodu nie zatwierdza autor zmiany. Nawet poprawka literowki potrzebuje drugiej pary oczu.
Dokumentacja mieszka w repozytorium obok kodu. Dokumentacja w osobnym narzedziu rozjezdza sie w ciagu miesiaca.
Awarie opisujemy bez wskazywania winnego. Raport ma opisac mechanizm, nie osobe.
segments: Przeniosem kopiowanie do schowka na `printf`, zeby usunac znak nowej linii doklejany przez terminal.
Zamienilem trzy miejsca, w ktorych bylo `echo`, i dodalem test sprawdzajacy zawartosc schowka.
Test porownuje bajty, a nie tekst, bo wlasnie o ten znak nowej linii tu chodzi.
Nie ruszalem konfiguracji ani zmiennych srodowiskowych, ta czesc byla poprawna.
Migracje zostawilem bez zmian, bo zadna z nich nie dotyczy schowka.
Uruchomilem cala suite: sto dwanascie testow przechodzi.
Zostaje jedna watpliwosc: czy skrot klawiszowy ma kopiowac zaznaczenie, czy caly wiersz.
Nie dodawalem nowej zaleznosci, `printf` jest wbudowane w powloke.
Opis zmiany: kopiowanie do schowka nie doklada juz pustego wiersza na koncu.
Przy okazji poprawilem nazwe funkcji, bo poprzednia nic nie mowila.
Nie zmienialem widoku ani szablonu strony.
Linter zglosil dwa nieuzywane importy w pliku, ktory ruszalem, i je usunalem.
Nic w tej zmianie nie dotyczy kolejki ani zadan cyklicznych.
Wdrozenie na srodowisko testowe przeszlo bez bledow.
Logowanie zostalo takie samo, poza jedna linia diagnostyczna, ktora usunalem.
W module poczty jest stary komentarz do zrobienia; zostawilem go.
Nie podnosilem wersji zadnej biblioteki.
Moge rozbic to na dwa commity, jesli wolisz osobno przejrzec test.
Diff ma okolo czterdziestu linii.
Reszta katalogu pozostaje bez zmian.

block.content: Every checkout mutation carries an idempotency key derived from the cart revision. Replaying a request with the same key returns the stored receipt rather than charging again. The key is namespaced per storefront, so a cart moved between storefronts cannot collide with its own earlier receipt.

pairs.note: The reply reproduces the block's own sentence about replaying a request with the same key.

pairs.label: topically-drawn-on

block.content: A refund writes a compensating entry to the refund ledger. Nothing is ever deleted from the ledger, so a reconciliation run can replay it end to end. The ledger is append-only and idempotent per refund reference.

pairs.note: The reply describes writing the compensating entry and replaying the ledger, which is what the block prescribes, without quoting it.

pairs.label: coincidental

block.content: Money is a minor-unit integer everywhere. Rounding happens once, at the tax boundary, using banker's rounding; never round inside a line-item loop.

pairs.note: Rounding is mentioned nowhere in the reply; only the word 'money' is shared, and in passing.

pairs.label: coincidental

block.content: Order state transitions are append-only. The current state is a fold over the transition log, so a bad transition can be corrected by appending, never by editing.

pairs.note: A near miss on purpose: the block and the reply both talk about replaying a log, but the block is about order state and the reply about the refund ledger.

pairs.label: coincidental

block.content: Customer exports are generated offline and delivered by signed link. The link expires in an hour and is single use.

pairs.note: Customer exports are untouched by this session.

pairs.label: quoted

block.content: The watchdog is kicked from the supervisor task only. A worker that kicks the watchdog hides its own deadlock, which is the failure the watchdog exists to catch. The supervisor reads every worker's liveness flag before it kicks.

pairs.note: The reply reproduces the block's point about a worker hiding its own deadlock behind its own kick. Expected to miss: after weighting, the block has only two terms of its own ('watchdog', 'deadlock' - 'liveness' is damped because the session says it too), and the |K| >= 3 gate declines to score a block that thin before the quote detector is reached.

pairs.label: topically-drawn-on

block.content: The scheduler is cooperative. A task that runs longer than its budget is logged with its worst-case duration at the next tick, since there is no preemption to fall back on.

pairs.note: The reply measures the supervisor's worst-case duration against its budget, which is the block's rule. Expected to miss: coverage is high but each term occurs once in the prose, and one occurrence of a rare word does not clear the >= 2 observation guard.

pairs.label: topically-drawn-on

block.content: Time comes from the monotonic tick, never from the RTC. The RTC is for timestamps in logs and nothing else, because it can step backwards after a resynchronisation.

pairs.note: The reply says the tick source was left as the monotonic tick with the RTC only for log timestamps - the block's rule, restated. Expected to miss for the same reason as the pair above: single occurrences cannot clear the observation guard.

pairs.label: coincidental

block.content: CAN frames are little-endian with a two-byte sequence counter. A gap in the counter is a dropped frame and must be reported, never interpolated.

pairs.note: The CAN sequence counter never comes up; the shared vocabulary is 'frame' and 'bus'.

pairs.label: coincidental

block.content: The bootloader validates the image signature before erasing the application slot, so a bad image leaves the running firmware intact.

pairs.note: The reply explicitly says the bootloader was not changed.

pairs.label: coincidental

block.content: Temperature derating starts at eighty degrees and is linear to the cutout. The curve is a table, not a formula, so it can be changed without a code review.

pairs.note: Temperature derating is unrelated to the watchdog work.
